headline: High: Firecrawl can exfiltrate web/API data while OpenBBTerminal can ingest it via MCP, creating default-path leakage and cascading trust risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Firecrawl ingests web content and exposes MCP-compatible outputs; OpenBBTerminal uses MCP and can consume external inputs. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path if Firecrawl-sourced content is treated as trusted by OpenBBTerminal. The pair lacks documented provenance isolation, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal parses Firecrawl output as instructions or tool directives
IF Firecrawl returns attacker-controlled web text that is forwarded through MCP without provenance tagging
mitigations: Add a strict allowlist for fields passed from Firecrawl to OpenBBTerminal
Strip or escape instruction-like text before forwarding outputs
Require a human review step for any web-derived prompt content
Log source provenance on every MCP message
requires-engineering: implement content-type separation between data and instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: Firecrawl touches API keys and broad web content, while OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data and can use MCP. If the pair shares an MCP bridge or workspace, Firecrawl can expose sensitive inputs to its external APIs and OpenBBTerminal can then surface them in downstream outputs. The default networked Firecrawl side makes leakage materially plausible.
conditions: IF Firecrawl is given API keys or other secrets in pages it scrapes
IF OpenBBTerminal receives Firecrawl-derived content containing financial or licensed data through MCP
IF either agent is configured to forward raw context to an external service
mitigations: Do not pass secrets into Firecrawl jobs
Disable or restrict MCP forwarding between the agents
Redact API keys and account identifiers before scraping
Use separate workspaces and credentials for each agent
requires-engineering: add DLP checks on all inter-agent payloads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Firecrawl supports multiple instances and broad network egress, while OpenBBTerminal supports multiple instances and MCP access to mutable financial workflows. Even though OpenBBTerminal cannot write files or modify git state, overlapping concurrent access to shared APIs or localhost services can still cause race conditions and inconsistent state. The interaction is plausible but not maximally destructive.
conditions: IF both agents target the same upstream API account or localhost service
IF concurrent runs share mutable credentials, caches, or rate limits
mitigations: Run the agents under separate API credentials
Serialize access to shared upstream services
Set per-agent rate limits and quotas
Use distinct cache directories and temp paths
requires-engineering: add distributed locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl produces extracted web content and OpenBBTerminal can consume MCP/API inputs for financial workflows. If OpenBBTerminal treats Firecrawl output as authoritative, a bad scrape or poisoned page can cascade into incorrect analysis or actions. Because the pair lacks built-in verification in the profiles, the safer choice is high rather than medium.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal uses Firecrawl output without independent verification
IF Firecrawl scrapes stale, manipulated, or adversarial web pages
mitigations: Require source citation checks before using scraped facts
Compare Firecrawl results against a second source
Mark scraped content as untrusted in OpenBBTerminal
Add a manual approval step before any downstream action
requires-engineering: implement confidence scoring and provenance tracking

E_compliance.rationale: Firecrawl touches web content and API keys, while OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data. That combination can create retention, residency, or licensing mismatches if Firecrawl-collected content is stored or forwarded into OpenBB workflows. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the gap is real but not proven severe.
conditions: IF Firecrawl stores or forwards scraped personal or licensed content into OpenBBTerminal
IF retention or deletion policies differ across the two systems
IF regulated data is processed without a DPA or equivalent controls
mitigations: Classify data before sending it between agents
Avoid routing licensed or personal data through Firecrawl
Set short retention windows on both systems
Document residency and retention responsibilities
requires-engineering: align compliance controls and audit logging
